children: The annual inflation rate in North Macedonia rose by 2.6% in August 2026 from a two-year low of 2.3% in the previous month.

Costs increased for clothing and footwear (2.1% vs 1.8% in July), housing utilities (3.8% vs 3.6%), health (1.5% vs 1.3%), transportation (3.4% vs 1.1%), information and communication (1.9% vs 2.0%), recreation and culture (8.8% vs 5.7%), education (5.0% vs 4.9%), and restaurants and hotels (4.8% vs 4.4%).
Moreover, price growth remained steady for miscellaneous goods and services (at 1.9%).

In contrast, inflation moderated for alcoholic beverages and tobacco (9.4% vs 9.5%), food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.0% vs 1.1%), furniture and household equipment (1.7% vs 2.1%), and insurance and financial services (0.3% vs 1.6%).
On a monthly basis, consumer prices grew by 0.4% in August, following a 0.1% gain in the preceding period.

title: North Macedonia Inflation Rises to 2.6% in August
